newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian natural monopolies not to be broken up - PM.
newsitem.headline: Russian natural monopolies not to be broken up - PM.

text.p: Russian natural monopolies are important and will not be broken up, Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin told the State Duma lower house of parliament on Friday.
"These systems (natural monopolies) are the backbone of the state... If someone thinks that they will be broken up, they are thinking in vain -- that is not going to happen," he said.
Chernomyrdin said that the government did not intend to cut energy and natural gas companies into pieces but added that the monopolies needed "fundamental reform".
"We are talking about something else -- an end to unjustified spending, cross subsidies, factoring (future) inflation in tariffs," said Chernomyrdin.
He was formerly in charge of Russia's natural gas industry, which became Gazprom, one of Russia's largest and richest companies.
Chernomyrdin said that the government plans for natural monopolies included increasing regulation, including of prices, and stopping cross-subsidisation.
Chernomyrdin said that the natural monopolies would be "cleaned" of social functions, with the exception of branches in the far north and deep within Siberia.

"We need to look at what expenses we are including in tariffs -- today they have their own hospitals and farms. Why does the Railroads Ministry have its own hospitals and stores in Moscow? What -- are there no stores in Moscow?" he said.
"We need to clean the natural monopolies of all that. And cleaning them up, we only help the natural monopolies."
But he said the government would have to be careful with the industries, which contribute 40 percent of federal income, he said.

The IMF has insisted on reform of Russian natural monopolies, including Gazprom GAZP.RTS, oil product pipeline company Transneft and national power utility Unified Energy System (UES) EESR.RTS as part of a Russian economic plan.
But Russia and the International Monetary Fund so far have not agreed a plan for the year, which is a condition for disbursements of tranches of a 3-year, $10 billion loan.
First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov has been given natural monopoly reform as part of his portfolio in a new reform-oriented government being formed.
